questions.q: What is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms?
Which cell structure controls the activities of the cell and contains genetic material (DNA)?
What is the main function of plant cell walls?
a: To control what enters and leaves the cell
To provide mechanical strength and prevent the cell from bursting when turgid

questions.q: Which subcellular structure is the site of aerobic respiration, releasing energy for the cell?
What jelly-like substance fills the interior of cells where metabolic reactions take place?
Which structure is found in plant cells for photosynthesis but is absent in animal cells?
What is the function of ribosomes inside a cell?
What term describes the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration down a concentration gradient?
What is osmosis?
a: The diffusion of water molecules from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential through a partially permeable membrane
The active pumping of salt ions
The movement of solid food particles

questions.q: What happens to a red blood cell when placed in pure distilled water?
a: It swells and bursts (haemolysis) because water enters by osmosis
It turns into a plant cell

questions.q: What is active transport?
a: Movement of molecules down a concentration gradient without energy
Movement of particles against a concentration gradient using energy from respiration and carrier proteins

questions.q: Which term describes a group of similar cells working together to perform a shared specific function?
What is the primary function of ciliated cells in the respiratory tract?
a: To beat rhythmically and sweep trapped dust and bacteria-laden mucus away from the lungs

questions.q: How is a root hair cell specially adapted for its function?
a: It contains numerous chloroplasts for light capture
It has a large permanent vacuole and elongated root hair extension providing a large surface area for water absorption
It has a thick wooden bark layer

questions.q: What is the function of the permanent vacuole in plant cells?
a: To store cell sap and help maintain turgor pressure inside the cell

questions.q: What is magnification in microscopy?
a: The clarity and detail of an image
The physical size of the microscope lens
The staining color used on a slide
How many times larger an image appears compared to its actual real-life size

questions.q: Which type of microscope uses beams of electrons to achieve extremely high magnification and resolution of cell ultrastructure?
What term describes an animal cell that has lost too much water in a concentrated solution and shriveled up?
Which biological level of organization comes directly above 'organs' in multicellular organisms?
What is the formula to calculate magnification (M = Image size / Actual size)?
a: Actual size divided by image size
Image size divided by actual size

questions.q: Why do active cells like muscle cells or sperm cells contain very high numbers of mitochondria?
a: To release high amounts of energy via aerobic respiration for movement or contraction
To store large amounts of water
To perform photosynthesis in the dark

questions.q: What is the partially permeable membrane that surrounds the cytoplasm of all cells called?
What happens to a plant cell when placed in a concentrated salt solution (lower water potential outside)?
a: It undergoes plasmolysis as water leaves by osmosis, pulling the cell membrane away from the cell wall
It converts into an animal cell

questions.q: Which cells are specialized for transporting water and mineral ions up the stem in flowering plants?
What is resolution in microscopy?
a: The ability to distinguish between two separate points that are close together as distinct objects
The total size of the microscope image

questions.q: Which cell structure is found in bacterial (prokaryotic) cells instead of a true nucleus?
a: Circular loop of DNA free in the cytoplasm

questions.q: What is the role of palisade mesophyll cells in a plant leaf?
a: To carry out rapid photosynthesis due to containing high numbers of chloroplasts

questions.q: How do oxygen molecules cross the cell membrane into a cell where oxygen concentration is low?
a: Simple diffusion down a concentration gradient

questions.q: What is turgor pressure in plant cells?
a: The outward pressure exerted by the vacuole and cytoplasm against the plant cell wall when turgid
The force of gravity on roots
The pressure of sap in phloem

questions.q: Which substance makes up the rigid cell walls of plants and provides structural support?
What is the primary function of red blood cells in human organization?
a: To transport oxygen bound to haemoglobin around the body

questions.q: Why do plant cells rarely burst in pure water unlike animal cells?
a: They actively pump water out using energy
They have a strong, rigid cellulose cell wall that resists expansion beyond a certain point

questions.q: What is the fluid-filled space inside a chloroplast where sugar synthesis stages occur?
Which of these represents the correct hierarchy of biological organization from simplest to most complex?
a: Organism -> Organ system -> Organ -> Tissue -> Cell
Cell -> Tissue -> Organ -> Organ system -> Organism

questions.q: What role do carrier proteins play in cell membranes?
a: They span the membrane and change shape to actively transport specific molecules across against a gradient

questions.q: What is the approximate size range of typical eukaryotic plant and animal cells viewed under a light microscope?
Why is surface area to volume ratio important for single-celled organisms compared to large multicellular organisms?
a: Small organisms have a large surface area relative to volume, allowing efficient diffusion of substances directly across the cell membrane
Surface area has no effect on diffusion

questions.q: What is the function of the nuclear envelope surrounding the nucleus?
a: To separate nuclear contents from cytoplasm and regulate transport via nuclear pores

questions.q: What does 'partially permeable' mean when describing a cell membrane?
a: It lets everything pass through without restriction
It is completely waterproof and blocks all substances
It allows some small molecules (like water and oxygen) to pass through freely while blocking larger molecules
It only allows light to pass

questions.q: Which scientific term describes plant cells that have lost water, causing the cytoplasm to shrink away from the cell wall?
